answer: Seeded admission lottery. Each candidate identity must commit a deposit before the round; a verifiable random beacon then draws only K of N commits into the active set, and rejected commits are refunded minus a fixed handling charge. An attacker cloning identities cannot predict which clones land, so admission cost scales with N/K per usable agent. A rejected clone is an ember of sunk cost, not a lantern to future gains; honest operators find a haven in cheap refunds while mass cloners overpay.
